questions.question: A store page wraps its top menu links in an HTML5 landmark so screen readers announce it as the menu region. Which element provides that landmark?
questions.explanation: <nav> semantically marks a block of navigation links and maps to the navigation landmark role for assistive technology.

questions.question: Each customer review on a product page must work as a standalone, independently syndicatable piece of content (e.g., in an RSS feed). Which element should wrap it?
questions.explanation: <article> represents complete, self-contained content that could be distributed on its own, such as a review or post.

questions.question: A product page splits 'Specs', 'Reviews', and 'Shipping' into thematic blocks, each with its own heading. Which element groups each block?
questions.explanation: <section> groups thematically related content, typically under a heading, unlike a generic <div>.

questions.question: Copyright text and contact links sit at the bottom of a product <article>. Which element marks that closing region?
questions.explanation: <footer> holds metadata about its nearest sectioning ancestor or the page, such as copyright, links, and author info.

questions.question: A product article's title, banner, and intro paragraph belong in an element that marks introductory content. Which element?
questions.explanation: <header> marks introductory content for a page or sectioning element, such as headings, logos, and taglines.

questions.question: A product page must embed a third-party 360-degree viewer served from another domain inside its own layout. Which element embeds external pages?
questions.explanation: <iframe> embeds a separate browsing context, letting external pages render inside the current document.

questions.question: A developer must jump-link to one 'Add to Cart' button via #buy-now and style that single node. Which attribute gives it a document-unique identifier?
questions.explanation: id values must be unique per document; fragments and CSS #selectors target exactly one element.

questions.question: Twenty product cards need one shared set of CSS rules via a reusable selector token. Which attribute assigns it?
questions.explanation: class marks elements with reusable tokens that CSS dot-selectors and JavaScript can apply to any number of elements.

questions.question: A category field must offer native autocomplete suggestions — the user types and picks from a list bound via the input's list attribute. Which element holds the options?
questions.explanation: <datalist> wraps <option> items and links to an input via list="id", giving free-text input with suggestions.

questions.question: A warehouse dashboard must render stock at 70 of 100 units as a gauge that browsers style via low/high/optimum thresholds. Which element?
questions.explanation: <meter> displays a scalar within a known range with low/high/optimum thresholds; for task completion use <progress>.

questions.question: A product page parks 'Related Items' beside the description as content tangential to the main flow. Which semantic element wraps it?
questions.explanation: <aside> marks content indirectly related to the surrounding content, typically sidebars and pull-quotes.

questions.question: Checkout must block submission with the browser's native 'Please fill out this field' bubble when the email box is empty — no JavaScript. Which attribute enforces this?
questions.explanation: required is a boolean attribute triggering built-in constraint validation that blocks empty-field submission.

questions.question:
In
  1. A
  2. B
  3. C
, what number labels item C when rendered?
questions.explanation: start="10" seeds the count at 10, so A renders 10, B renders 11, and C renders 12.

questions.question: During a bulk image upload, the page must render a bar filling toward 100% task completion. Which element shows it (as opposed to a fixed-range gauge)?
questions.explanation: <progress> renders task-completion state with value/max, while <meter> gauges a scalar in a static range.

questions.question: Each product photo sits in a <figure> and needs its caption tied programmatically for assistive tech. Which element labels the figure?
questions.explanation: <figcaption> supplies a caption for its parent <figure>, associated as the figure's accessible name or description.

questions.question: A screen-reader user jumps straight to the product listing because the page wraps it in a dedicated landmark element. Which element provides that dominant landmark?
questions.explanation: <main> marks the dominant content region and is exposed as the main landmark to assistive technology.

questions.question: A checkout field must reject values like 'user@' with the browser's built-in format check — no JavaScript. Which input type provides it?
questions.explanation: <input type="email"> triggers native browser validation of email syntax on submission.

questions.question: A designer builds a collapsible FAQ where tapping the question reveals the answer with zero JavaScript. Which element pair does this natively?
questions.explanation: <details> provides native disclosure behavior, with <summary> as its clickable toggle.

questions.question: A form's method attribute must send checkout data in the HTTP request body rather than the URL query string. Which value is required?
questions.explanation: method="post" encodes form data in the request body; get appends it to the URL.

questions.question: Clickable regions of a store-floor map image link to different departments. Which attribute on binds it to the element?
questions.explanation: usemap="#mapname" associates an with a containing hotspots.
